purpose: Hand-reviewed atomic facts for the three shortest character pages at cutoff 2, so that a prompt or extraction change can be judged on supported facts recovered rather than on raw accepted count or page length. docs/vision/plans/0006 work package A.
method: Every paragraph the recorded claim_extract requests carried for these three subjects was read (19, 22 and 42 paragraphs respectively), from data/spice-and-wolf/01_parsed only. No fandom page and no model was consulted. Labels are one reviewer's judgement, not adjudicated gold.
separate_from: docs/eval/gold -- this fixture has no floors and must not be added to any ratcheted benchmark.

status_values.already_covered: a claim carrying this fact exists and renders; finding it again is not a gain
status_values.covered_with_defect: a claim exists and renders, but says something the quote does not support
status_values.missing: supported by the quote, no claim carries it
status_values.must_not_assert: the page must NOT state this; `forbidden_value` names the value that constitutes the violation, so a claim that states the OPPOSITE correctly is not scored as one

splits.dev: may be used to design a change
splits.holdout: judge a change on these only after it is frozen

facts.subject: saint-metrogius
facts.quote: It’s the pilgrimage road of Saint Metrogius.
facts.note: Rendered as Titles: Saint.

facts.subject: saint-metrogius
facts.quote: you follow the path of Saint Metrogius in business
facts.note: Rendered as Role: saint of business. Loose predicate fit -- the text gives a way of doing business named for him, not an occupation he held. Lost by the 2026-09-24 re-extraction; the quote still supports it. Needs re-judging.

facts.subject: saint-metrogius
facts.quote: as I recall, you follow the path of Saint Metrogius in business, like your teacher did, correct?
facts.note: Lawrence and his teacher both follow the path -- a fact about Metrogius's reach among merchants. MUST NOT be encoded as MENTOR_OF/STUDENT_OF: the teacher in this sentence is Lawrence's own master. The extractor did produce STUDENT_OF and `wiki verify` withheld interval i_e7bc8913 for exactly this reason.

facts.subject: saint-metrogius
facts.quote: Perhaps it’s the protection of Saint Metrogius that’s kept my travels safe and my business sound.
facts.note: Reported belief, spoken by Lawrence and hedged with 'perhaps'. Any encoding must keep it attributed, never asserted as fact.

facts.subject: saint-metrogius
facts.quote: It’s the pilgrimage road of Saint Metrogius.
facts.note: A named road exists, travelled from Poroson toward Ruvinheigen. Held out: not used to design any prompt change.

facts.subject: saint-metrogius
facts.quote: they trod the paths of the saints of old
facts.note: The page ships 'Status: alive (assumed)'. Nothing in v1-2 states that he lives, and 'saints of old' points the other way. This is the open STATUS default conflict in docs/vision/plans/0006, not an extraction gap.

facts.subject: saint-ruvinheigen
facts.quote: there were records of Saint Ruvinheigen having red hair
facts.note: Deduplication control, per docs/vision/plans/0006. Already on the page via the window pass; re-finding it through scenes is not a recall gain. 2026-09-27 v1-5 re-extraction: no claim covers the red hair any more (was c_9c8ccf3e); a recall loss.

facts.subject: saint-ruvinheigen
facts.quote: Saint Ruvinheigen was said to have lost his left arm
facts.note: Kept `presumed`, and the prose renders 'According to historical records'. Correct: p0151 calls the tale possibly 'pure fabrication'. A change that flattens this into a plain assertion is a regression, not a gain. Lost by the 2026-09-24 re-extraction; the quote still supports it. Needs re-judging.

facts.subject: saint-ruvinheigen
facts.quote: in his battles against the heathen deities
facts.note: His defining action. Nothing on the page says he fought anyone.

facts.subject: saint-ruvinheigen
facts.quote: on the great mural in the city cathedral he was pictured with no left arm, his ragged clothing smeared with blood, resolutely ordering his crusaders forward against the pagans
facts.note: How he is depicted, and that he led crusaders. Reported via the mural, so the evidence is about the depiction.

facts.subject: saint-ruvinheigen
facts.quote: In the holy city of Ruvinheigen, there were records of Saint Ruvinheigen
facts.note: A relation to a LOCATION that has its own codex entry. The page's Relationships section names only Holo.

facts.subject: saint-ruvinheigen
facts.quote: The march was timed to coincide with the birthday of Saint Ruvinheigen
facts.note: Unhedged, and it drives the volume's plot. Held out: not used to design any prompt change.

facts.subject: saint-ruvinheigen
facts.quote: sinking my teeth into that Ruvinheigen’s backside
facts.note: Reaches the page as an INBOUND claim whose subject is Holo. A subject-only witness view calls this absent; it is not. 2026-09-27 v1-5 re-extraction: now a BACKGROUND claim on Holo ('bit the rear of Saint Ruvinheigen'), still on the page.

facts.subject: saint-ruvinheigen
facts.quote: Holo had set out on her travels hundreds of years ago
facts.note: The same STATUS conflict as M6: the page ships 'alive (assumed)' for a man Holo bit centuries earlier.

facts.subject: count-ehrendott
facts.quote: the noble who managed the land, one Count Ehrendott
facts.note: Rendered as Titles: Count.

facts.subject: count-ehrendott
facts.quote: Count Ehrendott, who managed the region surrounding Pasloe
facts.note: Encoded as ORIGIN_FROM pasloe, so the page reads 'Pasloe -- From -- manages the region surrounding the city'. The qualifier is right and the display label contradicts it: nothing says he is FROM Pasloe. No predicate in config/extraction.yaml fits a governance relation. 2026-09-27 v1-5 re-extraction: now OCCUPATION 'manager of the region surrounding Pasloe'; the ORIGIN_FROM defect is gone.

facts.subject: count-ehrendott
facts.quote: was a famous area eccentric

facts.subject: count-ehrendott
facts.quote: who enjoyed working in the fields himself
facts.note: The specific behaviour, distinct from the label 'eccentric'. p0069 supplies why it is eccentric: 'almost none of them took a personal hand in the farming or sale of their product.' The prose states it today, but no claim carries it.

facts.subject: count-ehrendott
facts.quote: Naturally the festival also enjoyed his support
facts.note: He backs the Pasloe harvest festival, which has its own codex entry.

facts.subject: count-ehrendott
facts.quote: Pasloe had come under the care of Count Ehrendott, and since then new farming techniques had been imported from the south, increasing yield
facts.note: The volume's causal hinge -- it is why Holo believes she is no longer needed. Held out: not used to design any prompt change.

facts.subject: count-ehrendott
facts.quote: The figure backing the Medio Company is Count Ehrendott!

facts.subject: count-ehrendott
facts.quote: The count and the merchants that deal with his wheat are the reason silver is being collected.
facts.note: Held out: not used to design any prompt change.

facts.subject: count-ehrendott
facts.quote: Most vineyard owners were noble, but almost none of them took a personal hand in the farming or sale of their product.
facts.note: The claim OCCUPATION 'vineyard manager' (c_4b8930fd) is a misattribution: the vineyard belongs to the unnamed noble of Perenzzo whom Lawrence is speaking to, and Ehrendott appears only as the contrast case. `wiki verify` already withholds it, so it does not render. A change that restores it to the page is a precision regression.

2026-09-24.reason: Commit b4b04c6 put polarity and qualifier into make_claim_id, so every claim_id changed the first time the graph was rebuilt after it. Only the pointers moved: each stale id resolved to exactly one claim with identical subject, predicate, target, first_vol, polarity and qualifier. No reviewed judgement, quote, status or split was touched. tests/test_character_evidence_coverage.py caught the staleness.

2026-09-24-re-extraction.reason: Adding `qualifier_disqualifiers` to SPOUSE_OF changed config, and extract/adequacy.py::prompt_rules() injects the gate config INTO the extraction prompt, so every claim_extract call was a cache miss and the claim set was re-rolled, not merely re-filtered. A config edit of this kind is never a surgical change. 2 pointers moved to a uniquely-matching claim (qualifier paraphrased, same paragraph and polarity); 2 facts disappeared from the graph entirely and are recorded as lost rather than re-pointed.
